why: The #778 identity-mark glyph strokes a fixed hue instead of `currentColor`, so it no longer takes its colour from the chip it sits in: under High contrast a green slot-1 chip carries an amber glyph, and the glyph cannot follow any palette (issue #1057). Killed by the test that requires every paint the glyph uses to be the chip colour, and already by #778's forced-colours case, which refuses any literal colour in the glyph.
killedBy: hud: identity mark in the stock strip (issue #778) paints on currentColor, so forced colours repaints it instead of dropping it
hud: stock chips in the session's owner palette (issue #1057) the identity-mark glyph takes its hue from the chip, so it follows the palette too (#778)
